Date of Institution of Petition : 09-08-2024 Nature of Petition : U/Sec.166 of MV Act.
Date of Commencement of : 12-06-2025 Recording of Evidence Date of pronouncement of : 28-03-2026 Judgment Total Duration : Year Months Days  01 07 19  JUDGMENT

The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 23-07-2024 at about 6.15 p.m. he was crossing the road near TIN Factory Bus Stop, Tin Factory, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657 drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, suddenly came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Govt. Hospital, K.R. Puram,
Bengaluru, after first aid he has shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient from 24-07-2024 to 30-07-2024.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries of left midshaft femur fracture with crush injury of left great toe and other injuries.
He underwent the procedure of CRIF with ILN femur.
Accordingly, the petitioner was spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 24 years, he was working as a Car Washer at Speedi Shine Smart Wash Service and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m.
Due to the accident, the petitioner is unable to do any work as he was doing prior to the accident.

5. It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence act of the rider of the Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657, against whom the K.R. Puram Police have registered the case in Cr.No.193/2024 P/U/Sec.125(a) and 281 of BNS.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the Owner and respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
6. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court through their respective counsel, but, respondent No.1 has not filed his objections to the main petition.
Respondent No.2 has filed its objections to the main petition.

7. Respondent No.2 in its objection contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
2 on facts and hence, it is liable to be dismissed in limine.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy.

It is further contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle did not have effective and valid DL to drive the same and as such respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further contended that, there was no negligence on the part of the alleged driver of the alleged insured vehicle in issue as he was proceeding with due care and cautious by following traffic rules and regulations.

It is further contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself who was crossing the Road without observing the on coming vehicle, where there is no permissible crossing.

Further, Respondent No.2 has denied the accident,
age, income and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

8. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 23-07- 2024 at about 6.15 PM, he was crossing the road near Tin Factory Bus Stop, Tin Factory, Bengaluru,
at that time, all of a sudden a Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657 driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, came at high speed, dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to forced impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3) What order or award?

9 . In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 13 and got examined the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked 02 documents as per Ex.P.14 and P.15.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any oral evidence and not marked any documents on their sides.

10. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials available on hand.
11.
For the following reasons, this Tribunal given answer to the above Issues as under:-

Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
3 12 . ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident, that occurred on 23-07-2024.
13.
The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R. Ex.P.2 is the copy of Complaint,
Ex.P.3 is the copy of Police Intimations, Ex.P.4 is the copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the copy of Sketch, Ex.P.6 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.7 is the copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 is the copy of Charge Sheet, Ex.P.9 is the copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.10 is the Reply to the Notice, Ex.P.11 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P.12 is the medical bills and Ex.P.13 is the copy of Aadhar Card.
In the cross-examination he has denied that, the accident was took place due to his negligent act.
14. The petitioner got examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. who is an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho And Dental Senter, Bangalore is examined as PW.2 and got marked 02 documents as Ex.P.14 and 15.

entities.text: Sai Ortho And Dental Senter, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P.14 is the Clinical Examination Report and Ex.P.15 is the X-ray.
15. Per contra, the respondents have not adduced any evidence and got marked no documents on their side.
16. Learned counsel for petitioner submitted his arguments by contending that, the accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, prayed to award the compensation.
Counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted his arguments contending that, due to the negligent act of the petitioner the accident took place.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the petition.

Ld.
Counsel for respondent No.2 has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in ILR 2000 KAR 3443, between United India Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. D.C. Rajanna & Another and in 2020(4) KCCR 2621, between Sri. Nandish K. Vs. United India Ins. Co. Ltd., & Another with respect to the consideration of functional disability.

entities.text: United India Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. D.C. Rajanna & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sri. Nandish K. Vs. United India Ins. Co. Ltd., & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said judgments have been considered during the assessment of disability.
18. Respondent No.2 has contended that due to the negligence on the part of petitioner himself, the alleged accident has taken place and therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation.
As per Ex.P.4 and 5 the Mahazar and Sketch, the accident took place on the old Madra road of Tin factory to K.R.Pur.
It is contended that the accident occurred while petitioner was crossing the road.
The vehicle and other users of the road including the pedestrian are required to follow the traffic rules.
If the incident occurred in the highway, the vehicle will have right of way and the person who would like to cross the road is required to take proper precaution and cross the road.
But, the situation in the city limits is totally different.
In the city limits, the constant moving of the people in the city limits is usual and permissible.
The specific zebra crossing is provided for the pedestrian to cross the road and normally people shall opt for it.
But in the present case, it is not the case of the respondents that zebra crossing or Sky walk was available near the place of occurrence.
Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to prove the same.

Therefore, it cannot be said that the petitioner was prohibited from crossing the road at the place of occurrence as it is within the city Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
4 limits.
Such being the case, it was the duty of the driver of the offending vehicle to notice the petitioner and tried to avoid the accident.
It is not even contended that the petitioner suddenly entered the road.
Therefore, the evidence on record is clear that driver of the offending vehicle has failed to take reasonable care to protect the petitioner.
The driver of the offending vehicle was expected to recognize the petitioner on the road and he should have slow down his vehicle.
This omission of the driver of offending vehicle constitutes the negligence on his part.
After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, this Tribunal hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle.

19. On perusal of Ex.P.1-the FIR, Ex.P.2-the Complaint, Ex.P.3-the Police Intimation, Ex.P.4-the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5-the Sketch, Ex.P.6-the IMV Report, Ex.P.8-Charge Sheet, Ex.P.9-Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act and Ex.P.11- Reply to the Notice, it appears that, the driver of the Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.

On perusal of Ex.P.5-Spot sketch and Ex.P.8-Charge sheet, it appears that, on the date of accident,
driver of the offending Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at very high speed and dashed the petitioner and caused the accident.
As per Sketch the petitioner was crossing the road and came at the middle of the road and driver of the offending vehicle came at high speed and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
There is an enough space towards the right side of the offending vehicle.
If driver of the offending vehicle took his vehicle on right side then the accident would have been avoided.

Therefore, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657, so it clearly indicates that the offending vehicle involved in the accident.

Further on perusal of charge sheet it discloses that, the K.R. Puram Police have filed the case against the driver of Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657 for the offence punishable U/Sec.281 and 125(b) of BNS.
Further, there is nothing on record to show the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
20. Therefore it is clear that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

For the purpose of disproving proving the sole negligence of the petitioner,
nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.
Further, the owner of offending vehicle has not challenged the charge sheet.

21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/ Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

entities.text: 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. Respondent No.2 took contention that the respondent No.1 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but respondent No.2 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of considered opinion that respondent No.2 has Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
5 not proved that respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

23. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-the FIR, Ex.P.2-the Complaint, Ex.P.3-the Police Intimation,
Ex.P.4-the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5-the Sketch, Ex.P.6-the IMV Report, Ex.P.8-Charge Sheet,
Ex.P.9-Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act and Ex.P.11-Reply to the Notice, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the rider of Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner produced wound certificate at Ex.P.7 issued by Govt. Hospital, K.R. Puram, Bangalore and Ex.P.11 discharge summary issued by Sri. Atal Behari Vajpayee Medical College and Research Institute, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.

entities.text: Atal Behari Vajpayee Medical College and Research Institute, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The respondents not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.7, it is discloses that, the petitioner has sustained (1) Left great toe avulsed, (2)
Abrasion at right side abdomen, (3) Abrasion at right lateral thigh, (4) Abrasion at left knee joint, (5)
Abrasion at left lateral avulsion, (6) Abrasion at right forearm and (7) Abrasion at left dorsum.
On perusal of the said injuries, the Doctor has opinion that the injuries are simple and grievous in nature.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.11 discharge summary, wherein the diagnosis that, left midshaft femur fracture with crush injury of left great toe and procedure was done for CRIF with ILN Femur and admitted on 24-07-2024 and discharged on 30-07-2024.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, as petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and admitted in the hospital, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
25. The petitioner produced medical bills, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per the said bills, the petitioner has spent Rs.25,607/- towards medical expenses.
The respondents have not made out any grounds to disbelieve the medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.25,607/- under the head of medical expenditure.
26. As per Ex.P.11 discharge summary the petitioner took treatment at Sri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Medical College and Research Institute, Bangalore from 24-07-2024 to 30-07- 2024 for 07 days.

entities.text: Atal Bihari Vajpayee Medical College and Research Institute, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.10,500/- under the head Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
27. The Petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Doctor Sri.Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.2 deposed that, on 26-06-2025 the petitioner came to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination he found that, the petitioner has wasting of the left thigh muscles, restricted left hip and knee movements and the recent X-ray of the left femur shows united fracture with implant in-situ.

He examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically and assessed the total disability of the left lower limb at 47% and the whole body disability of the Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
6 petitioner at 16%.
In the cross- examination admitted that, he has not the treated doctor, he has seen the discharge summary and wound certificate of Bowring Hospital.
As on 26-06-2025 the fracture is united with implants in situ.
Since, the petition is 25 years old the disability may decrease in future.
However by considering the nature of the wounds, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the Petitioner at 11% to the whole body.

28. The petitioner stated that, at the time of accident he was aged about 24 years and he was doing Car Washing Work at Speedi Shine Smart Wash Service and he used to earn a sum of Rs.30,000/-
p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot do any work as earlier.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
Therefore, in present days the coolie worker get Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.
This accident is of the year 2024.

However, by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/-.
29.
As per Ex.P.13 Notarized Copy of Adhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is 22-05-2000.
Therefore, age of the Petitioner is taken as 24 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 18 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,500 x 12 x 18 x 11% = Rs.3,92,0400/-
Hence, this Tribunal award Rs.3,92,040/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
30.
The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief- examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, he is forced to spent huge amount for future medication.
PW.2 doctor deposed in the chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implants and the estimate of said surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
In the cross-examination the PW.2 admitted that he had not treated the petitioner and fractures are united.

However, by considering the age and nature of injuries and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head future medical expenses (Which does not carry any interest).

31. The petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was working as Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- pm and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to attend the work and facing financial difficulties.
The petitioner had not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
This accident occurred in the year 2024.

However, by considering the age and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Tribunal awarded reasonable compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.
32. The petitioner sustained grievous injury as shown in the wound certificate.
The petitioner was doing Coolie work and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
7

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

33. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
Sl.
 Under the Heads Amount No.
 1. Pain and sufferings Rs. 60,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs. 25,607/-
 3. Transportation, Nourishment, Rs. 10,500/-
 Conveyance and Attendant  charges.
 4. Compensation on account of Rs. 3,92,040/-
 permanent disability  5. Towards future medical Rs. 20,000/-
 expenses  6. Loss of income during laidup Rs. 30,000/-
 period.
 7. Towards loss of amenities of Rs. 30,000/-
 life
Total Rs
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,68,147/-.
34. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this Court has hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.

35. Liability:-
Respondent No.1 is the Owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending Bolero Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-48/A-3657.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Vilas vs Hanumanth Madar on 28 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67620136/
8 offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
36. ISSUE No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,68,147/- with interest @ 6% p.a.,(excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification(as petitioner has to incurred some more amount for medical expenses).
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

Such being the case, it was the duty of the driver of the offending vehicle to notice the petitioner and tried to avoid the accident.
It is not even contended that the petitioner suddenly entered the road.
Therefore, the evidence on record is clear that driver of the offending vehicle has failed to take reasonable care to protect the petitioner.
The driver of the offending vehicle was expected to recognize the petitioner on the road and he should have slow down his vehicle.
This omission of the driver of offending vehicle constitutes the negligence on his part.
After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
Therefore, this Tribunal hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, there is nothing on record to show the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
For the purpose of disproving proving the sole negligence of the petitioner,
nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.
21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/ Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
22. Respondent No.2 took contention that the respondent No.1 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but respondent No.2 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, as petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and admitted in the hospital, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.
Hence, this Court has hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
